title: Overbooking races and payment edges
idea: A hotel overbooks when two overlapping stays both see a free night and both take it; the fix makes each night's check and take one atomic step.

analogy.text: Two clerks read the same paper ledger, both see one room left on the 14th, and both write a name. One ledger line per night, locked while written, stops it.
analogy.breaks: A stay needs several lines at once; a clerk writes one.

points: Stays overlap on some nights, so the race hides in one shared night.
Check-then-act across nights lets both threads pass the check before writing.
Take each night with compare-and-set, in sorted order, and give back on failure.
A payment timeout has an unknown outcome: keep the hold, retry, same key.

hero.title: Two stays, one room on the 14th

steps.caption: Unsafe version. G-7 checks nights 13 and 14 while G-9 checks 14 and 15.
Both checks pass. Nobody has written yet, so the 14th looks free to both.
G-7 writes its two nights and reports success.
G-9 writes on its stale yes. The 14th now has two guests for one room.
Safe version. Each thread takes its nights in sorted order with `compareAndSet`.
G-7's CAS on the 14th lands first and moves its count from 0 to 1.
G-9's CAS sees 1, which equals capacity, so it fails. Its 15th was never taken.

code.title: Prove the race
code.caption: A barrier makes both threads check before either writes, so the overbooking shows up on every run.

walk.text: Run the same race twice: check-then-act first, then per-night CAS.
One counter per night and a barrier for exactly two threads.
G-7 wants the 13th and 14th; G-9 wants the 14th and 15th.
Unsafe: check every night, wait for the other thread, then write.
Safe: take nights in sorted order; on failure, give back what was taken.
`compareAndSet` writes only if nobody changed the count since it was read.

code.title: Expiry, timeout, cancel
code.caption: Times are passed in, so expiry and retries replay the same way every run.

walk.text: RS-1 holds the last room; RS-2 is refused, then wins after the sweep.
A late payment, a gateway timeout, a retry with the same key, then a cancel.
The fake gateway charges, then times out once. A known key replays its result.
The sweeper frees holds that are unconfirmed and past their deadline.
Confirm is idempotent and refuses an expired hold.
A timeout keeps the hold: the charge may have gone through.
Cancelling a confirmed reservation gives the room back to inventory.

pitfalls: Do not release nights on a payment timeout; the charge may have succeeded.
Lock or take nights in one sorted order, or two stays can block each other.
Run the expiry sweeper on a schedule; expiring only on the next read leaves rooms stuck.

quiz.q: What is the first line NightRace prints?
options: per-night CAS: winners 1, night 14 taken 1 of 1
quiz.why: The barrier waits until both threads have checked. Both saw the 14th free, so both write and the shared night is sold twice.

takeaway: Make check and take one atomic step for every night of a stay.

starters: Why sort the nights before taking them?
Would one lock per room type be simpler than per-night CAS?
How long should a hold wait for a payment with an unknown outcome?
